entry.title: Twenty-three Deity Nairatma Mandala
entry.blurb: A mandala is a diagram of a realm of enlightened beings.

source.credit: The Cleveland Museum of Art. Purchase from the J. H. Wade Fund

facts: The outermost ring contains depictions of eight cremation grounds, where corpses burn, and dogs and vultures feed on human remains.
Buddhist practitioners spend time in cremation grounds in order to overcome fear of death and attachment to their physical bodies.
A practitioner can then reach the splendid realm of eternal bliss in the center.

candidate.title: Twenty-three Deity Nairatma Mandala
candidate.medium: Gum tempera, ink, and gold on cloth
candidate.credit: The Cleveland Museum of Art. Purchase from the J. H. Wade Fund
candidate.description: A mandala is a diagram of a realm of enlightened beings. This mandala depicts the palace of Nairatma, who dances in the center. The outermost ring contains depictions of eight cremation grounds, where corpses burn, and dogs and vultures feed on human remains. Buddhist practitioners spend time in cremation grounds in order to overcome fear of death and attachment to their physical bodies. A practitioner can then reach the splendid realm of eternal bliss in the center. Accomplished teachers guide a practitioner’s meditations through the cremation grounds and every section of the mandala. Virupa is depicted twice, always pointing to arrest the sun with his raised left hand. He sits among the lineage masters along the top edge, and is also depicted in the topmost segment of the ring of cremation grounds, being served a cup of liquor.
